doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sinatra, Shirley Horn and film songs
title: Letting songs write themselves
summary: Mandel says he lets songs write themselves, wrote The Shadow in about fifteen minutes in a restaurant, and prefers melody away from the piano rather than fitting a chord pattern.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Um-hm, it’s one of those songs that’s a little, not obscure but it’s… yeah, it’s not very well known, it’s one of those songs a little like, “You are There,” in the sense that the two songs aren’t similar but they tend to go in unproven paths. I just let that song write itself, I didn’t try to construct any particular kind of song and the same with, “You are There,” they just sort of came out that way and I let them go. Which I think is really the best way to write.
I think Bob Brookmeyer said that, “a lot of times I don’t have too much control over these things.”
It’s much better if I don’t.
‘Cause it’s the only way I can get out of my own way. “The Shadow,” came out all like that, I wrote it in about fifteen minutes, “Emily,” too.
Yeah, sure, wrote, “The Shadow,” in an all night restaurant back in the good ol’ days before they had music everywhere. When you could go into a place and get silence.
So you wrote it in a restaurant, does that mean that you do a lot of your song writing away from the piano?
Songwriting yes. I think that’s the best way to write your songs, I think a good song will hold up, a capella, a bad song will not. That’s one of the rules I have.
Yeah, now that I think of it, some of the songs I’ve written, I’ve written the melodies first and added the chords later.

Yeah, I mean I used to do what a lot of other people did, get a chord pattern and then fit the melody over it, that’s what’s wrong with most pop tunes of the day. It’s, you know, they’ll get a riff, they’ll get a chord pattern and they’ll just bebop over it you know and write – and then the melody to fit the chords and such, that is not songwriting.
At least not by my kind of…
Now-a-days you’re lucky if the songs have chords.
You’re very lucky if they have chords, or if they have more than two or three. Most of them don’t, I just decided never to pay attention to that.
